name: Real Analysis
strandNote: Not needed to be hired. Quant researcher at firms that hire maths PhDs; reading proofs in papers.
description: Prove why calculus works, from the real numbers to compactness.

requires.why: Uses contradiction and direct proof to show sqrt 2 is irrational and that rationals are dense.
Uses limits by eye, computing limits and behaviour far out; the derivative itself is not needed for sequences.
Proves the comparison and ratio tests that taylor level 3 only used without proof.
Proves Rolle's theorem and the mean value theorem that limits level 5 used from the flat tangent.
Proves the fundamental theorem of calculus that integrals level 2 derives with the strip argument.
Length from the dot product and perpendicularity help with norms in metric examples; only a little is used.

lessonNames.l11-partial-sums: A series as a limit of partial sums
lessonNames.l17-extreme-value: Maximum and minimum on a closed interval
lessonNames.l18-mean-value-proved: The derivative and the mean value theorem proved

lessonObjectives.l1-gaps-in-the-rationals: Show that the rationals have gaps, such as a missing square root of 2.
lessonObjectives.l2-least-upper-bound: Find the supremum and infimum of a set, and prove a number is one.
lessonObjectives.l3-completeness: State the completeness axiom and use it to prove that $\sqrt{2}$ exists as a real number.
lessonObjectives.l4-archimedes: Prove the Archimedean property and that the rationals are dense in the reals.
lessonObjectives.l5-counting-infinite-sets: Show that the rationals are countable and, by the diagonal argument, the reals are not.
lessonObjectives.l6-epsilon-and-n: Prove that a sequence converges using the epsilon and N definition.
lessonObjectives.l7-limit-laws-proved: Prove the limit laws for sums and products, and that a convergent sequence is bounded.
lessonObjectives.l8-bounded-and-monotone: Prove that a bounded monotone sequence converges, and use it on a recursive sequence.
lessonObjectives.l9-subsequences: Prove that every bounded sequence has a convergent subsequence.
lessonObjectives.l10-cauchy: Prove that a sequence converges exactly when it is Cauchy.
lessonObjectives.l11-partial-sums: Define a series’ sum as the limit of its partial sums, and prove that terms of a convergent series tend to zero.
lessonObjectives.l12-convergence-tests: Prove and use the comparison, ratio and integral tests.
lessonObjectives.l13-absolute-conditional: Tell absolute from conditional convergence, and prove the alternating series test.
lessonObjectives.l14-rearranging: See why rearranging a conditionally convergent series can change its sum.
lessonObjectives.l15-epsilon-delta: Prove a function is continuous with the epsilon and delta definition, and link it to sequences.
lessonObjectives.l16-intermediate-value: Prove the intermediate value theorem from completeness.
lessonObjectives.l17-extreme-value: Prove that a continuous function on a closed interval attains its maximum and minimum.
lessonObjectives.l18-mean-value-proved: Prove Rolle’s theorem and the mean value theorem from the definition of the derivative.
lessonObjectives.l19-uniform-convergence: Tell pointwise from uniform convergence, and prove that a uniform limit of continuous functions is continuous.
lessonObjectives.l20-riemann-integral: Define the Riemann integral with upper and lower sums, and prove that continuous functions are integrable.
lessonObjectives.l21-fundamental-theorem-proved: Prove the fundamental theorem of calculus.
lessonObjectives.l22-metric-spaces: Check the metric space axioms for several distances, and rewrite convergence with them.
lessonObjectives.l23-open-and-closed: Prove a set is open or closed, and characterise closed sets by limits of sequences.
lessonObjectives.l24-compactness: Prove that closed bounded intervals are compact and that continuous functions on compact sets are bounded.
